nodes.ask: Agitated, withdrawing or in a mental health crisis in the ED. First moves?
options: A safe room and enough staff; vitals with temperature, oxygen and glucose
IM haloperidol and lorazepam at once, before anyone takes the vital signs
A urine drug screen and alcohol level before anyone examines the patient
Four-point restraints first, then vital signs once the patient is still
nodes.chainStep: Enough trained staff and a room with dangerous objects removed and a clear exit; approach at 2 arm's lengths; vital signs with temperature, oxygen saturation and fingerstick glucose as safety allows; a brief history from police, EMS and family; mental health triage alongside physical triage
nodes.why: Agitation can come from a medical illness, so a brief history and vital signs come first where it is safe, with the oxygen level and the blood sugar; abnormal vital signs or glucose call for immediate evaluation by a clinician (BETA). The clinician keeps at least 2 arm's lengths away with a clear exit, and staff stay close. Routine labs and drug screens do not come first: the history and examination find most medical illness, and a urine drug screen seldom changes the ED disposition (AAEP 2017; ACEP rated routine screening unnecessary, Level C). Unless the patient is actively violent, restraint does not come before de-escalation. Medicine is chosen once a likely cause is known, and NICE asks for mental health triage alongside physical triage.

orders.dose: Brief history and vital signs, with oxygen level and fingerstick glucose; abnormal vital signs or glucose need immediate clinician evaluation

Agitation that persists once these are corrected starts this pathway again.

A medical cause leads: head injury goes to the trauma pathway (pw_trauma), a new focal deficit to the stroke pathway (pw_stroke), and fever with a stiff neck or a source to the sepsis and fever pathway (pw_sepsis_fever). New agitation is presumed medical until proven otherwise; sedate only as safety demands while the cause is treated, checking oxygen and glucose at once if restraint is needed.

nodes.chainStep: Continuous monitoring; active external cooling; IV fluids; IV benzodiazepine titrated until agitation and autonomic signs settle; CK, creatinine and electrolytes; stop any dopamine blocker or serotonergic drug; intubation if cooling and sedation fail
nodes.why: Benzodiazepines are first line for stimulant agitation and, in StatPearls, for anticholinergic agitation (pw_tox gives physostigmine first when the QRS is narrow), titrated until the agitation and autonomic instability settle, and they lower heart rate, muscle tone, temperature and seizure risk; hyperthermia predicts deterioration, so external cooling starts at once. Fighting against restraints drives rhabdomyolysis, which calming with a benzodiazepine helps prevent. An antipsychotic can be the cause: neuroleptic malignant syndrome follows dopamine blockers, haloperidol most often, and its first treatment is stopping them. Dantrolene is kept for severe neuroleptic malignant syndrome, and its benefit there is uncertain.

nodes.summary: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: every dopamine blocker stopped, ICU care with aggressive cooling, fluids and electrolyte correction, benzodiazepines for agitation, and bromocriptine or dantrolene for severe cases (doses not in the sources read). Most recover in 2 to 14 days; an antipsychotic is restarted no sooner than 2 weeks after recovery, as a lower-potency agent at a low dose, without lithium.

A toxidrome with hyperthermia: serotonin toxicity, stimulant toxicity or anticholinergic delirium. The toxicology pathway (pw_tox) takes it from here, with its own doses. Stimulant agitation gets IV benzodiazepines titrated to effect with external cooling. For anticholinergic delirium the sources differ: StatPearls gives IV benzodiazepines first and physostigmine for cases refractory to them, while pw_tox gives physostigmine first (label) when the QRS is narrow. Lithium toxicity also belongs to pw_tox.

Unless the patient is actively violent, restraint does not come before talking.

All restrained patients are monitored, and medication is given to calm them.

nodes.summary: Delirium or dementia with agitation: the altered mental status pathway (pw_ams) takes it from here, with the cause search, the 4AT, and short-term low-dose haloperidol only when de-escalation fails. Antipsychotics carry a boxed warning for increased death in older people with dementia-related psychosis, haloperidol is contraindicated in Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies, and benzodiazepines can worsen delirium unless it comes from alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal (BETA).
No acute medical or psychiatric cause found: home once settled and sober, with follow-up for any mental health or substance need, and the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.

Intoxication settling: observe until sober, with breathing and consciousness checked every 15 minutes if rapid tranquillisation was needed, look for injury, hypoglycemia and co-ingestion, and reassess mental state, suicidal thoughts and capacity when sober; after self-harm, a breath or blood alcohol level does not delay the psychosocial assessment (NICE). An overdose or a toxidrome goes to the toxicology pathway (pw_tox), and withdrawal signs bring the patient back to this pathway's withdrawal route.

Tests are directed by the likely diagnosis rather than done routinely, and other neurologic causes come into play with seizures or delirium. Electrolytes including magnesium and phosphate are checked and replaced. Clonidine and beta blockers only mask the signs and prevent neither seizures nor delirium tremens.

Glucose raises thiamine needs, so thiamine goes in before or with glucose when feasible, but treatment of significant hypoglycemia is never delayed for it. Low magnesium blunts recovery, so it is replaced.

nodes.summary: Imminent suicide risk with voluntary admission: psychiatric admission with observation, lethal means removed, and the specific risk factors the stay can change addressed. Risk rises sharply in the 3 months after discharge from a psychiatric unit and the year after an ED visit, so follow-up contact is arranged.

Imminent risk and refusing care: an involuntary hold for evaluation under the local law, which generally requires a severe mental illness, a significant risk of harm to self or others and no less restrictive option. Keep the patient in sight meanwhile. Patients keep their rights, including the least restrictive treatment and the ability to appeal; details vary by state and are not in this pathway.

No imminent risk: a collaborative safety plan (warning signs, coping strategies, people and services to contact, lethal means restriction), firearms stored safely or transferred and medicines secured with family, follow-up contact after the visit, a mental health referral, and the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. In a VA ED cohort, safety planning with telephone follow-up lowered suicidal behavior at 6 months (3.03% against 5.29%).

Agitation or confusion with a high temperature after heat exposure or exertion, no drug or withdrawal: heat stroke until proven otherwise. The environmental pathway (pw_environmental) takes it, with cooling first.

cases.label: Agitated drinker with a low glucose
cases.vignette: 51-year-old man, a heavy drinker, brought by police shouting and swinging at staff; sweaty and tremulous. HR 112, BP 138/84, RR 18, SpO2 97% on air, T 36.8 °C (98.2 °F).

results.front: Fingerstick glucose 42 mg/dL (2.3 mmol/L); no injury seen; pupils equal and reactive.

cases.label: Combative after a fall on apixaban
cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman on apixaban, confused and combative after a fall at home. HR 92, BP 162/90, SpO2 96%, T 36.9 °C (98.4 °F).

results.front: Glucose 118 mg/dL; scalp hematoma; GCS 14 with a new left arm drift.

cases.label: Rigid and febrile after a haloperidol increase
cases.vignette: 34-year-old man with schizophrenia; haloperidol increased 4 days ago; now confused, agitated, sweating and stiff. HR 128, BP 172/104, RR 24, SpO2 96%, T 40.1 °C (104.2 °F).

results.front: Glucose 102 mg/dL; drenched in sweat; lead-pipe rigidity in all limbs; no injury.
results.hot_cause: Rigidity without clonus or hyperreflexia; no serotonergic drugs or stimulants; CK 18,400 U/L, WBC 16,000/µL, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL.

cases.label: Hot and agitated after cocaine
cases.vignette: 26-year-old man, shouting and pacing after a night out; says he used cocaine. HR 146, BP 188/110, RR 26, SpO2 98%, T 39.6 °C (103.3 °F).

results.front: Glucose 132 mg/dL; drenched in sweat, pupils 7 mm, tremulous; no rigidity; no injury.
results.hot_cause: Sweating with big pupils after cocaine; brisk reflexes without clonus; no antipsychotic or serotonergic drug.

cases.label: Febrile withdrawal delirium
cases.vignette: 58-year-old man; stopped drinking 3 days ago; now confused, picking at the air. HR 138, BP 176/102, RR 24, SpO2 95%, T 38.9 °C (102 °F), weight 78 kg.

results.front: Glucose 96 mg/dL; drenched in sweat, coarse tremor, disoriented; neck supple; no cough, urinary symptoms or wound; no focal signs.
results.hot_cause: Visual hallucinations, disoriented to place and date; last drink 3 days ago; no antipsychotic, serotonergic drug or stimulant; no clonus or rigidity.

cases.label: Violent relapse of schizophrenia
cases.vignette: 29-year-old man with schizophrenia, off risperidone for a month; shouting that staff are poisoning him and throwing a chair. HR 104, BP 142/88, SpO2 98%, T 37.0 °C (98.6 °F).

results.front: Glucose 96 mg/dL; no injury, focal signs or rigidity; no smell of alcohol.
results.deesc_result: Keeps advancing on staff despite one calm voice; refuses oral olanzapine; security staff hold him.
results.cause: Calm 30 minutes after the injection; persecutory delusions and voices as in his past relapses; attentive and oriented; denies suicidal thoughts; normal neurologic exam.
results.psych_result: Vital signs and cognition normal; glucose and electrolytes normal; the same picture as his past relapses.

cases.label: Violent and intoxicated
cases.vignette: 38-year-old man from a bar fight, punching the walls and threatening staff; smells of alcohol. HR 98, BP 136/82, SpO2 97%, T 36.7 °C (98.1 °F).

results.front: Glucose 108 mg/dL; knuckle abrasions, no head injury; no focal signs.
results.deesc_result: Slurred and ataxic, spitting at staff despite de-escalation; no tremor or sweating; breath alcohol high; security staff hold him.
results.cause: Settling and drowsy but rousable; no tremor or sweating; denies suicidal thoughts; no other injury.

cases.label: Violent in early alcohol withdrawal
cases.vignette: 47-year-old man who stopped drinking 30 hours ago when his money ran out; pacing, sweating, swinging at a nurse. HR 122, BP 168/98, SpO2 97%, T 37.5 °C (99.5 °F).

results.front: Glucose 112 mg/dL; tremor and sweating; no injury, no rigidity.
results.deesc_result: Strikes out again despite one calm voice; no hallucinations or delusions; not drunk; refuses oral medicine; security staff hold him.
results.cause: Calmer after lorazepam; oriented; coarse tremor and sweats; last drink 30 hours ago; no hallucinations.
results.aws_sev: CIWA-Ar 18; a withdrawal seizure 2 years ago; liver tests near normal.
results.aws_resp: CIWA-Ar 9 at 4 hours; pulse 96; calm and talking.

cases.label: New mania that is thyrotoxicosis
cases.vignette: 52-year-old woman with no psychiatric history; 5 days without sleep, talking fast, spending her savings, shouting in triage. HR 124, BP 148/78, SpO2 99%, T 37.4 °C (99.3 °F).

results.front: Glucose 104 mg/dL; fine tremor, warm moist skin; no rigidity or clonus; no injury.
results.deesc_result: Settles with one calm voice in a quiet room and agrees to stay.
results.cause: Pressured speech and grandiosity; first episode at 52; attentive and oriented; no suicidal thoughts; lid lag and a goiter.
results.psych_result: TSH under 0.01 mIU/L with a high free T4; urine drug screen negative; pregnancy test negative.

cases.label: Mild withdrawal, wants to stop
cases.vignette: 36-year-old man who wants to stop drinking; last drink 14 hours ago; anxious and shaky. HR 98, BP 138/86, SpO2 99%, T 36.9 °C (98.4 °F).

results.front: Glucose 98 mg/dL; mild tremor; calm and cooperative.
results.cause: Oriented; mild tremor; drinks 8 beers a day; no hallucinations.
results.aws_sev: CIWA-Ar 6; no past seizures or delirium tremens; no other sedatives; his sister will stay with him; electrolytes and magnesium normal.

cases.label: Withdrawal in cirrhosis that escalates
cases.vignette: 61-year-old man with compensated cirrhosis, no ascites; last drink 36 hours ago; sweating and tremulous. HR 118, BP 158/92, SpO2 96%, T 37.4 °C (99.3 °F), weight 70 kg.

results.front: Glucose 88 mg/dL; tremor; cooperative; no injury.
results.cause: Oriented; coarse tremor and sweats; spider naevi, no jaundice; no hallucinations.
results.aws_sev: CIWA-Ar 21; no past seizures; bilirubin 1.8 mg/dL, albumin 3.2 g/dL, INR 1.4.
results.aws_resp: Two hours later: disoriented and hallucinating despite repeated lorazepam; HR 134.

cases.label: Withdrawal seizure in the ED
cases.vignette: 42-year-old woman; last drink 20 hours ago; tremulous and anxious in triage. HR 112, BP 150/94, SpO2 98%, T 37.2 °C (99 °F).

results.front: Glucose 104 mg/dL; tremor; cooperative.
results.cause: Oriented; tremor and sweats; drinks a bottle of vodka a day; no hallucinations.
results.aws_sev: While being scored: a generalized tonic-clonic seizure for 1 minute; awake and oriented 15 minutes later; glucose 104 mg/dL; no head injury; her seizures have only ever come with withdrawal.
results.aws_resp: CIWA-Ar 7 by the evening; no further seizures.

cases.label: Withdrawal delirium found on the history
cases.vignette: 55-year-old man brought by family; stopped drinking 3 days ago; now confused and seeing insects. HR 124, BP 164/98, SpO2 97%, T 37.6 °C (99.7 °F), weight 82 kg.

results.front: Glucose 110 mg/dL; tremulous and sweating; neck supple; no injury.
results.deesc_result: Calmer with one calm voice and oral lorazepam 2 mg; still picking at the sheets.
results.cause: Disoriented to place and date, inattentive, visual hallucinations; last drink 3 days ago; tremor.

cases.label: Wernicke encephalopathy
cases.vignette: 49-year-old woman, a heavy drinker, thin, vomiting for a week; confused and unsteady. HR 102, BP 112/70, SpO2 98%, T 36.6 °C (97.9 °F).

results.front: Glucose 84 mg/dL; calm and cooperative but confused.
results.cause: Horizontal nystagmus and weak abduction of both eyes; wide-based gait; inattentive; little tremor; last drink yesterday.

cases.label: Benzodiazepine withdrawal
cases.vignette: 33-year-old woman who ran out of alprazolam 2 mg three times daily 3 days ago; shaking and panicky. HR 116, BP 150/92, SpO2 99%, T 37.3 °C (99.1 °F).

results.front: Glucose 92 mg/dL; tremor; no injury or fever.
results.deesc_result: Settles with one calm voice; sits and talks.
results.cause: Daily alprazolam for 2 years, stopped abruptly; tremor, anxiety, insomnia; no alcohol; oriented.

cases.label: Heroin withdrawal, buprenorphine works
cases.vignette: 27-year-old man using heroin daily, last use 16 hours ago; wants treatment. HR 104, BP 142/88, SpO2 99%, T 37.1 °C (98.8 °F).

results.front: Glucose 96 mg/dL; restless but cooperative.
results.cause: Yawning, runny nose, gooseflesh, pupils 6 mm, cramps; not sedated; breath alcohol zero.
results.cows_result: COWS 14; last heroin 16 hours ago; no methadone.
results.bup_result: COWS 9 two hours after 4 mg, so another 4 mg; an hour later COWS 3, alert and comfortable.

cases.label: Precipitated withdrawal after the first dose
cases.vignette: 31-year-old woman who smokes fentanyl daily, last use 13 hours ago; wants treatment. HR 110, BP 136/84, SpO2 99%, T 37.0 °C (98.6 °F).

results.front: Glucose 90 mg/dL; uncomfortable but cooperative.
results.cause: Gooseflesh, yawning, runny nose, big pupils; not sedated.
results.cows_result: COWS 13; last fentanyl 13 hours ago; no methadone.
results.bup_result: Forty minutes after 4 mg: vomiting, drenched in sweat, gooseflesh; COWS 24.

cases.label: On methadone, too early to switch
cases.vignette: 40-year-old man on methadone 60 mg daily who wants to switch to buprenorphine; last methadone dose 10 hours ago. HR 84, BP 128/80, SpO2 99%, T 36.8 °C (98.2 °F).

results.front: Glucose 94 mg/dL; calm.
results.cause: Mild yawning only; pupils 4 mm; not sedated.

cases.label: Acute dystonia after an antiemetic
cases.vignette: 19-year-old man given IV prochlorperazine for vomiting at another ED yesterday; now his neck twists to the right and his eyes are forced upward. HR 96, BP 128/76, SpO2 99%, T 36.8 °C (98.2 °F), weight 68 kg.

results.front: Glucose 100 mg/dL; distressed but cooperative; speaking clearly, no stridor.
results.cause: Sustained neck twisting and upward eye deviation; alert and oriented; no fever or rigidity.

cases.label: Akathisia mistaken for agitation
cases.vignette: 24-year-old woman who started haloperidol 5 mg twice daily a week ago; pacing triage, says she feels she could jump out of her skin. HR 98, BP 124/78, SpO2 99%, T 36.8 °C (98.2 °F).

results.front: Glucose 96 mg/dL; pacing, shifting her feet; no rigidity, fever or injury.
results.deesc_result: Talks calmly with one clinician but keeps standing up and shifting her feet.
results.cause: Inner restlessness since haloperidol started; no new voices or delusions; no dystonia.

cases.label: Acute risk, wants to leave
cases.vignette: 45-year-old man brought by his wife after she found a goodbye note; quiet and withdrawn. HR 88, BP 132/80, SpO2 99%, T 36.7 °C (98.1 °F).

results.front: Glucose 102 mg/dL; calm and cooperative.
results.cause: Low mood for 2 months; the note; denies any ingestion; sober.
results.asq_result: Yes to questions 1 to 3; question 5: yes, he is thinking of killing himself right now.
results.eval_result: Plans to shoot himself with the handgun at home; demands to leave and refuses admission.

cases.label: Acute risk, agrees to admission
cases.vignette: 22-year-old woman who cut her forearm superficially tonight after a breakup; tearful. HR 90, BP 118/72, SpO2 99%, T 36.8 °C (98.2 °F).

results.front: Glucose 94 mg/dL; superficial cuts only; cooperative.
results.cause: Self-harm tonight; denies any ingestion; sober.
results.asq_result: Yes to questions 1 to 4 (an overdose at 17); question 5: yes, right now.
results.eval_result: Intends to take her mother's pills tonight; agrees to stay.

cases.label: Non-acute risk, safety plan
cases.vignette: 35-year-old man laid off last month, sleeping badly; says things feel pointless. HR 76, BP 124/78, SpO2 99%, T 36.7 °C (98.1 °F).

results.front: Glucose 99 mg/dL; calm.
results.cause: Low mood for a month; no self-harm; sober.
results.asq_result: Yes to question 1 (wished he were dead in recent weeks); no to questions 2 to 4; no to question 5.
results.eval_result: No plan, intent or past attempts; lives with his brother, who will keep his hunting rifles at his own house; wants outpatient help.

cases.label: Low mood, negative screen
cases.vignette: 40-year-old woman brought by her sister after a divorce; low mood. HR 80, BP 122/76, SpO2 99%, T 36.8 °C (98.2 °F).

results.front: Glucose 92 mg/dL; calm.
results.cause: Sad and tearful for a week; no self-harm; sober.

cases.label: Violent delirium in dementia
cases.vignette: 79-year-old woman with dementia, pulling at her IV and striking a nurse since this morning. HR 104, BP 150/84, SpO2 95%, T 37.6 °C (99.7 °F).

results.front: Glucose 140 mg/dL; no injury, focal signs or rigidity.
results.deesc_result: Keeps striking out despite one quiet voice; inattentive and fluctuating; no alcohol or sedatives; new dysuria.

cases.label: Shouting after an argument, no acute cause
cases.vignette: 27-year-old man shouting and pacing in triage after an argument with his partner; no drugs or alcohol today. HR 102, BP 138/84, SpO2 99%, T 36.8 °C (98.2 °F).

results.front: Glucose 98 mg/dL; no injury, focal signs or rigidity; breath alcohol zero.
results.deesc_result: Calms within minutes with one calm voice and a drink of water; declines medicine.
results.cause: Oriented and attentive; no psychosis, withdrawal or intoxication; denies thoughts of harming himself or anyone else; ASQ negative; normal exam.

cases.label: Agitated delirium in dementia
cases.vignette: 84-year-old man with dementia, hitting staff at his care home since yesterday; on donepezil. HR 96, BP 146/82, SpO2 95%, T 37.4 °C (99.3 °F).

results.front: Glucose 132 mg/dL; no injury or focal signs; no rigidity.
results.deesc_result: Calmer with his daughter at the bedside and one quiet voice.
results.cause: Inattentive and fluctuating since yesterday; positive 4AT; care staff report new dysuria.

cases.label: Confused after a long run in the heat
cases.vignette: 24-year-old man brought in from a summer half marathon, combative and confused at the finish line; no drugs, no medications, no alcohol. Weight 72 kg.

results.front: HR 138, BP 104/62, SpO2 97%, rectal temperature 41.2 °C (106.2 °F); glucose 108 mg/dL; skin hot; no rigidity or clonus; pupils normal.
